items.q: Cūr magnae nāvēs in Tiberī nāvigāre nōn possunt?
items.en: Why can't big ships sail on the Tiber?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (little water ...)

items.en: What kind of ships come to Rome?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative plural

items.en: What is Ostia?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a relative clause

items.en: Where is Ostia situated?
items.hint: accusative after 'ad' (at the mouth ...)

items.en: What is the sea-coast?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a genitive

items.en: How are people and goods carried?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative of means (by ...)

items.q: Quem adit is quī nāvigāre vult?
items.en: Whom does a man who wants to sail go to?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.en: When is the sea rough?
items.hint: a 'cum' clause (when ...)

items.q: Quālēs sunt flūctūs quōs tempestās facit?
items.en: What are the waves that a storm makes like?
items.hint: a comparative adjective in the nominative plural

items.en: Why do sailors fear storms?
items.hint: a reason: big waves can ... (infinitive with 'possunt')

items.en: What do the sailors wait for in the harbour?
items.hint: a noun with adjective in the accusative (the object)

items.en: What is the rear part of a ship called?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (a name)

items.en: Where does the helmsman sit?
items.hint: ablative after 'in' (place where)

items.en: What is the east?
items.hint: a phrase in the nominative with 'unde' (from where)

items.en: How many parts of the sky are there?
items.hint: a number in the nominative

items.en: From what is the north named?
items.hint: ablative with 'ā' (from ... stars)

items.q: Ad septentriōnēs nāvigantī, ubi est oriēns?
items.en: For someone sailing north, where is the east?
items.hint: ablative with 'ā' (on the ... side)

items.en: What is the sky like today?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative neuter

items.en: What is Medus (by nationality)?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.en: Where does Medus want to return to?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (motion towards)

items.q: Quid sēcum ferunt Mēdus et Lydia?
items.en: What do Medus and Lydia take with them?
items.hint: nouns in the accusative (the objects), with 'paulum' + genitive

items.en: Where does Lydia hide the book?
items.hint: ablative after 'sub' (under ...)

items.en: When does the ship leave the harbour?
items.hint: an ablative absolute (with the sun ...)

items.en: Who follows Medus onto the stern?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.q: Quid Mēdus et Lydia ex altā puppī spectant?
items.en: What do Medus and Lydia look at from the high stern?
items.hint: accusative noun with a present participle

items.en: Where is Medus going to?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (motion towards)

items.en: Whom does Medus no longer fear?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object of 'verētur')

items.q: Cūr Lydia Rōmam nōn sine lacrimīs relinquit?
items.en: Why does Lydia not leave Rome without tears?
choices: quia Rōma patria eius nōn est
items.hint: a reason: Rome is a second ... for her (dative)

items.q: Nōnne Lydia gaudet quod eī licet cum Mēdō venīre?
items.en: Isn't Lydia glad that she is allowed to come with Medus?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'nōnne' expects 'yes'

items.en: Why can't Lydia be glad?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (she is leaving ...)

items.en: Where do the tears fall from?
items.hint: ablative after 'dē' (down from ...)

items.en: In which direction are they sailing?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (towards ...)

items.en: What does Medus see above the sea?
items.hint: a noun with adjective in the accusative (the object)

items.en: Whom does the sailor fear?
items.hint: a name in the accusative (the object)

items.en: Why does the helmsman call on Neptune?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (he is lord of ...)

items.en: What is the ship like because of the goods?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.en: Does anyone comfort the sad merchant?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no' (nobody ...)

items.en: How is Medus's voice heard?
items.hint: an adverb (how)

items.q: Quis est dominus quem Lydia invocat?
items.en: Who is the lord that Lydia calls upon?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: Can anyone give Medus orders?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (nobody ...)

items.q: Cūr Mēdus nōn potest sē movēre?
items.en: Why can't Medus move?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (Lydia is holding ...)

items.en: What begins to drop?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)
